title: Adoption Rate of Cashless Transactions in Singapore
what_it_is: Adoption Rate of Cashless Transactions in Singapore

sections.label: PayNow and PayNow Corporate take-up
sections.summary: PayNow and PayNow Corporate registrations have grown since their launches, with 2.8 million individual registrations and over 115,000 UENs registered.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Since the launch of PayNow in July 2017 and PayNow Corporate in August 2018, take-up has been encouraging.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: There have been 2.8 million individual registrations for PayNow, of which 1.8 million are bank accounts linked to mobile phone numbers and the remainder are linked to National Registration Identity Card numbers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: We estimate that more than 65% of Singaporeans aged between 20 and 75 have already registered for PayNow, and the numbers are still increasing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: As for PayNow Corporate, over 115,000 unique entity numbers (UENs) have been registered.

sections.label: Transaction volumes and values
sections.summary: In July this year, volumes had increased to over five million transactions with total values over S$1 billion per month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In July this year, those volumes had increased to over five million transactions, with total values over S$1 billion per month.

sections.label: SGQR code deployment
sections.summary: Over 32,000 SGQR codes have been deployed across merchants including hawker centres, retail stores, food and beverage outlets, supermarkets and healthcare outlets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Since then, over 32,000 SGQR codes have been deployed across a range of merchants, including hawker centres, retail stores, food and beverage outlets, supermarkets and healthcare outlets.

sections.label: SGQR and terminals at stalls
sections.summary: SGQR labels and unified point-of-sale terminals have been deployed at over 500 stalls across 10 hawker centres, 22 coffee shops and 12 industrial canteens.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: To date, SGQR labels and unified point-of-sale terminals have been deployed at over 500 stalls spread across 10 hawker centres, 22 coffee shops and 12 industrial canteens.

sections.label: Cheque and ATM cash decline
sections.summary: Cheque volumes have reduced by 8% per year over three years, and ATM cash withdrawals relative to card and FAST payments fell from about 50% to 30%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Cheque volumes have been reducing by 8% per year over the last three years and automated teller machine cash withdrawals relative to card and Fast And Secure Transfers payments have fallen from about 50% three years ago to 30% over the same period.

sections.label: Promoting PayNow Corporate, charging cheques
sections.summary: The speaker agrees MAS should encourage banks to promote PayNow Corporate while charging for cheque use, noting take-up is fast and cheque use is dropping.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The take-up is fast and you see a corresponding drop in the use of cheques.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, I agree with the Member that the Monetary Authority of Singapore should encourage banks, and banks should also take the initiative, to promote PayNow Corporate, but at the same time we charge for the use of cheques.
